reforms.description: Japan reformed its R&D system to increase flows of information and researchers among government research laboratories, universities, and businesses. The reform introduced competitive considerations in budgetary allocation and made third-party evaluation of projects obligatory to improve the efficiency of public spending on research and technology.
reforms.package_name: Science Basic Plan and R&D System Reform
reforms.component_name: R&D System Integration and Competitive Allocation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Competitive allocation and third-party evaluation improve allocative efficiency and research productivity. Enhanced flows between sectors accelerate knowledge transfer and commercialisation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'The government improved' and 'implemented', indicating reforms were in force at time of survey.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant system-wide reform of R&D governance and funding mechanisms, but not a structural creation of new institutions.
reforms.source_quote: It has also taken initiatives to improve the hitherto compartmentalised R&D system, by increasing the flows of information and researchers among the government research laboratories, universities and businesses, and by enhancing the efficiency of R&D funding through the introduction of competitive considerations in budgetary allocation and the obligation of strict third-party evaluation of publicly funded projects.

reforms.description: Japan implemented the Science Basic Plan to promote an open and competitive R&D system, with emphasis on increasing basic research and improving the efficiency of public spending on technology.
reforms.package_name: Science Basic Plan and R&D System Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased basic research funding and improved efficiency of public R&D spending enhance long-term productivity and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan implemented the Science Basic Plan', indicating the plan was in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy initiative establishing a strategic framework for basic research, but not a structural institutional change.
reforms.source_quote: Science Basic Plan is being implemented to promote open and competitive R&D system (see Chapter IV). This is a promising start.

reforms.description: Japan strengthened intellectual property protection for innovators and encouraged universities to patent and commercialize their innovative work. The government revised patent-related laws and supported the establishment of Technology Licensing Offices (TLOs) to facilitate the transfer of university research to the market.
reforms.package_name: University Intellectual Property and Commercialisation Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthened IP protection and university commercialisation mechanisms increase incentives for innovation and accelerate technology transfer from research to market, supporting productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'The government strengthened' and 'Universities were encouraged', indicating reforms were in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reform of university-industry knowledge transfer mechanisms and IP regime, affecting the commercialisation pathway for public research.
reforms.source_quote: Universities are now encouraged to have their innovative work patented and sold through a Technology Licensing Office. As well, the patent-related laws have been revised to strengthen the protection of innovators' intellectual property rights.

reforms.description: Japan adopted measures to promote the establishment and growth of venture companies by improving the provision of private risk capital. Reforms included easing restrictions on pension fund investment in unlisted shares, creating a special over-the-counter (OTC) market for innovative companies, and implementing measures to facilitate transactions of unlisted shares, supported by financial deregulation.
reforms.package_name: Venture Capital and Risk Finance Reform
reforms.component_name: Venture capital infrastructure and unlisted share market development
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased availability of risk capital for innovative ventures supports the creation and scaling of new technology-based firms, enhancing entrepreneurship and innovation-driven growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Entry [2] states 'implemented'; entry [4] states 'announced'. Taking most advanced status: implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant financial and regulatory reform enabling venture capital supply, affecting the startup ecosystem and commercialisation of innovations.
reforms.source_quote: The government has readied the legal and institutional infrastructure for a leap in the supply of risk capital to finance new business ventures, including the easing of the restriction on investment in unlisted shares by pension funds, the creation of a special over-the-counter market for innovative companies, and measures to improve the transactions of unlisted shares.
